question: Which cold calls produced a follow-up, and what did the successful ones have in common?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract whether the call ended with a concrete follow-up (scheduled meeting, demo, trial, proposal sent, email or call back agreed, or none), and quote the relevant next-step statements. Also extract what the prospect said about their current situation, pain points, interest level, decision-making role, timing, and any objections or reasons for declining, plus what OrbitFlow staff offered or proposed in the call.
assumptions: 'Successful' is interpreted as cold calls that produced a concrete follow-up; the reader will report the follow-up status so the comparison can be made across calls.
Scope limited to Cold call type calls (CALL-016 to CALL-020).

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: I won't call you again this year. I'll send one email in February with something specific about Power Automate
findings.context: The call ended with an agreed one-email follow-up in February 2026 from OrbitFlow, with no call-back; the prospect accepted it conditionally. — Concrete next step is only an email, not a meeting, demo, or trial. Vendor promised no further calls this year; prospect agreed to one email.

findings.speaker: Dermot Kelly
findings.quote: February's fine. One email.
findings.context: Prospect agreed to receive the single February email. — Acceptance of the follow-up, but it is a minimal commitment; he did not agree to a meeting.

findings.speaker: Dermot Kelly
findings.quote: we finished an ERP migration in March and I've told everyone in this building that nobody is buying any new software this year.
findings.context: Prospect is not in buying mode: a recent ERP migration (March) and a company-wide statement that no new software will be bought this year. — Primary objection and reason for declining; timing is next year at earliest.

findings.speaker: Dermot Kelly
findings.quote: You're the fourth this month.
findings.context: Prospect has already been approached by several vendors this month (fourth), and is tired of cold outreach. — Suggests high vendor-solicitation volume; relevant to interest level.

findings.speaker: Dermot Kelly
findings.quote: it'd be me and it'd be our IT director jointly. And I'll tell you now, we've got Power Automate through our Microsoft deal, so it'd have to be pretty compelling.
findings.context: Prospect would co-own any workflow layer with the IT director, and already has Power Automate via the Microsoft deal, so a new tool must be 'pretty compelling'. — Decision-making role and main competitive objection; a stated reason to decline.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: The specific thing we usually fix is that nobody can see where something's stuck until it's late.
findings.context: OrbitFlow pitched fixing handoffs across systems managed over email and spreadsheets, where stuck work is only visible when late. — Vendor's value claim in the opening pitch; prospect said it 'lands' but did not confirm a pain point.

findings.speaker: Dermot Kelly
findings.quote: It lands. But we're not looking at anything.
findings.context: Prospect said the pitch resonated but that they are not evaluating anything now; interest level is low for this year. — Mixed signal: tone is polite, but the stated position is no active project.

findings.speaker: Martine Duval
findings.quote: Send me the page and copy Chloe. If the page is good she'll put it in the diary.
findings.context: The call ended with a concrete follow-up: Martine asked for a one-page document (not a deck) to be sent and asked Chloe to be copied so it can be put in the diary; Leo requested a 30-minute non-demo meeting in the week of the sixth, and Martine's reply routed that through the page. — Concrete next step agreed, but the meeting itself was conditional on the page being good; no date was confirmed.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: can I ask for thirty minutes in the week of the sixth? Not a demo. I'd want to understand the disruption process before I show you anything.
findings.context: Leo proposed a 30-minute meeting in the week of the sixth, explicitly not a demo, to first understand the disruption process. — Vendor offer; prospect did not explicitly accept the meeting date.

findings.speaker: Martine Duval
findings.quote: It's handled badly. It's handled by a very good team working very hard, which is not the same as handled.
findings.context: Martine said the disruption process (flight cancellation, rebooking, supplier notification, customer comms, refund/credit across four systems) is handled, but badly; it depends on a very good team working very hard. — Prospect describes a current pain point; she accepted Leo's description as accurate.

findings.speaker: Martine Duval
findings.quote: That is — yes. That's accurate.
findings.context: Martine confirmed that the disruption-event process described by OrbitFlow matches her operation. — Agreement with vendor's description of the problem.

findings.speaker: Martine Duval
findings.quote: She said three.
findings.context: Martine has a limited time window: she said the call should be three minutes, not five, and the call was cut short with a request to be sent material rather than a demo. — Timing constraint; she was busy with a supplier conference that week and had just come off another call.

findings.speaker: Chloe Barnes
findings.quote: She's the right person. She's also very busy this week — we've got a supplier conference.
findings.context: Chloe said Martine is busy this week because of a supplier conference and suggested calling back Thursday or Friday; Martine then took the call immediately after being asked. — Gatekeeper's initial timing objection, later overridden when Martine agreed to take the call.

findings.speaker: Chloe Barnes
findings.quote: If you say "workflow automation" she'll be polite for a minute and then get off. If you say something about our actual business she'll listen.
findings.context: Chloe advised that Martine responds to specifics about the business rather than generic workflow automation pitches. — Gatekeeper advice on what engages the decision-maker; the vendor's opener was generic.

findings.speaker: Chloe Barnes
findings.quote: She's the right person.
findings.context: Martine is the right person for operational process problems and is a Director of Customer Operations with decision-relevant authority over the process. — Gatekeeper confirmed the routing; Martine's role was confirmed by the participant list.

findings.speaker: Martine Duval
findings.quote: Alright — send me something. Not a deck. Something short that describes what you'd actually look at.
findings.context: Martine indicated she was interested enough to take the call and asked for a short written page, but did not commit to a meeting. — Moderate, conditional interest; the outcome depends on the page's quality.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Half an hour, in the next couple of weeks, with you and whoever owns the housing management system technically. I'd want to understand the systems and I'd want to ask about procurement properly. No demo.
findings.context: The call ended with a concrete follow-up: a meeting in the week of the sixth, with the prospect agreeing to send technical requirements and frameworks and to bring in Priya Menon. — Concrete next step agreed at the end of the call; the vendor's meeting is explicitly not a demo, and the prospect sets the timing.

findings.speaker: Ade Balogun
findings.quote: Alright. Send me the technical requirements, I'll send you the frameworks, and I'll get Priya. Week of the sixth?
findings.context: Prospect agreed to the next steps: vendor sends technical requirements, prospect sends frameworks list, and they meet the week of the sixth. — Mutual agreement to a follow-up meeting closing the call.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Then I'll check before we meet, and if we're not on any of them I'll tell you and we can decide whether it's worth continuing.
findings.context: Vendor committed to check whether OrbitFlow is on the prospect's procurement frameworks before the meeting. — Vendor action item tied to the follow-up.

findings.speaker: Ade Balogun
findings.quote: We cannot tell whether it's one property or a pattern. I've been asking for that for two years.
findings.context: Prospect is head of business change with a pain point: average void (empty property) turnaround of 26 days against a sector benchmark of about 18, and no way to tell whether delays are one-off or a pattern. — Prospect's current situation; the dashboard showed only the average.

findings.speaker: Ade Balogun
findings.quote: The housing management system and the repairs system have an integration that works about eighty percent of the time. Compliance is entirely manual.
findings.context: Current systems are fragmented: housing management system, separate repairs and compliance systems, email and spreadsheets; the HMS-repairs integration works about 80% of the time and compliance is entirely manual. — Technical context that affects fit and integration effort.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: There's a reasonable chance we don't have a native connector for it, and we'd be working through an API or building something.
findings.context: Vendor flagged that OrbitFlow likely has no native connector for the prospect's housing management system and may need API work at added cost; prospect had assumed as much. — Vendor objection-surfacing; a potential cost and effort barrier.

findings.speaker: Ade Balogun
findings.quote: Practically, anything meaningful goes through a framework or a tender, and a tender is nine months of my life.
findings.context: Procurement is a major barrier: the prospect buys through frameworks or tenders, and a tender takes about nine months. OrbitFlow has no housing association reference. — Objection on purchasing route and references; prospect deferred it to procurement.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Run it for eight weeks and look at where the time actually goes. Then automate the two stages that turn out to matter, rather than the eight stages people complain about.
findings.context: Vendor proposed a non-sale first phase: instrument the voids process with timestamps for about eight weeks, then automate only the stages that matter, and prospect saw it as cheaper. — OrbitFlow offer that narrowed the deal size; prospect engaged with it positively.

findings.speaker: Ade Balogun
findings.quote: Our technical person is Priya Menon — she's our applications manager.
findings.context: Prospect's applications manager Priya Menon is the technical decision-influencer and is skeptical of vendors; prospect will ask her to join. — Decision-making role; Ade is the champion and Priya will test the vendor.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: If we get to a demo and it turns out we can't be procured or can't reach your housing system, I've wasted an hour of your life and mine.
findings.context: Vendor said that a demo would be premature until procurement and system reach were confirmed. — OrbitFlow offer that the first meeting is discovery, not a demo.

findings.speaker: Ade Balogun
findings.quote: It was a much better cold call than I expected too. Bye.
findings.context: Prospect's view of the call was positive and interest was high, though the vendor repeatedly offered to end the conversation. — Interest level; the prospect's enthusiasm was inferred from tone and repeated engagement.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: is it worth me sending you some information, just so you've got it?
findings.context: The call ended with no meeting, demo, trial or call-back scheduled; the only next step was an information email the prospect said she would not read. — Vendor offered to send information; prospect explicitly said she would not read it and declined further follow-up attempts. No concrete follow-up agreed.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: I'll be honest with you, I won't read it.
findings.context: Prospect said she would not read the information and did not want repeated follow-ups. — Declining the offered send-over; preference to avoid being chased.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: Recruitment. Dental nurse recruitment. That's my biggest challenge and it has been for two years.
findings.context: Prospect's biggest challenge is dental nurse recruitment, not a process problem, and the vendor's onboarding automation pitch did not address it. — Prospect rejected the vendor's framing; recruitment is a pay/market issue.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: It's not a process problem, it's that nobody wants to be a dental nurse for what we can afford to pay.
findings.context: Prospect said the problem is not process-related; nobody wants to be a dental nurse at the pay offered. — Explicit reason she saw no fit for OrbitFlow.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: Eighteen hundred a month is not a number that exists in my world.
findings.context: Main objection is price: the vendor's entry package at 1800 pounds a month is far above what the group can afford; she would expect 200-300 a month and would need to justify it. — Prospect said price is the real problem even if the pitch had been better.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: you haven't asked me a single question about what we actually do.
findings.context: Prospect said the group is an 11-practice general dental group and the vendor's facts were wrong (14 practices, referrals direction, no knowledge of NHS e-Referral), and that the vendor did not ask about their operations. — Vendor pitch was generic; prospect corrected factual errors and criticized lack of discovery.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: There's a chap who comes in on Tuesdays.
findings.context: Prospect is not the decision maker for technology; the only other person mentioned is a part-time contractor who fixes printers, so no IT owner was identified. — Vendor asked for another contact; none was useful.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: Then we're not it.
findings.context: Prospect concluded OrbitFlow is not a fit and the vendor agreed to end the call. — Clear no; vendor accepted it.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: I'd have to check.
findings.context: Vendor's stated offer was to come in, review onboarding, compliance and referrals and automate them; the vendor also claimed integration with anything that has an API, but could not confirm the NHS e-Referral API. — Vendor product claim left unverified ('I'd have to check').

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Send me something short — not a deck — on how you'd approach the seven-stage thing, and specifically on the operations-can-change-it question.
findings.context: The call ended with a concrete follow-up: Leo agreed to send a short written note on the seven-stage approach and the operations-can-change-it question, and Rafael said he would do a thirty-minute call if the note was good; no meeting time was fixed. — Follow-up is conditional on the note being good; Rafael explicitly declined to restart the evaluation. Next step is an email, with a possible 30-minute call before mid-October.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Would it be worth a thirty-minute call before mid-October? Not a pitch.
findings.context: Leo proposed a thirty-minute call before mid-October, framed as non-pitch, to walk through how he would structure the seven stages. — Offered by vendor; prospect did not commit to a date at the time and conditioned it on the note.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Have someone in operations, not your developer, build one real workflow.
findings.context: Leo offered to run a test in which operations staff, not the developer, builds one real workflow, and suggested running it against Tray. — Vendor proposal to evaluate ops-owned change ability; vendor said it costs the prospect nothing.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Your name came up on a list and got crossed off.
findings.context: Prospect is a COO evaluating Tray.io with a decision date around mid-October and says he will not move it; OrbitFlow had earlier been crossed off his list because its website seemed enterprise-focused. — Interest is cautious; initial rejection was based on marketing perception, not product fit.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Tray don't have a connector and we're looking at building against its API, which our one back-end developer estimates at three weeks.
findings.context: Prospect's pain point: ERP integration lacks a Tray connector; his one back-end developer estimated three weeks, which he believes will be six. Process changes by operations may wait weeks. — Stated objection/pain relevant to fit; prospect declined to name the ERP.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: If it's a mid-market manufacturing ERP, we probably don't have a native connector
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff said they probably lack a native connector for the prospect's ERP, so the advantage on that point is none; they claimed only a subtler argument about maintenance and reuse. — Vendor candour; this is a concession, not a claim of superiority.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: a month is a month of revenue on a two hundred thousand pound order.
findings.context: Prospect quantified cost of delay: about a month of revenue on a £200k order, with eleven orders in flight. — Business impact relevant to urgency and board case.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Well. Genuinely well. Their team's been good.
findings.context: Prospect said the Tray evaluation is going well and they are three weeks in, which Leo cited as reason he would be a third option in a two-horse race. — Vendor argued against joining late; prospect framed interest as low in a cold call.

draft.answer: Four of the five cold calls ended with some follow-up: Beacon Housing Trust (a meeting), Silverline Travel and Kestrel Robotics (a short note that could lead to a call or meeting), and Quarry Ridge Foods (one email only) [C1][C2][C3][C4]. Trafford Dental Group produced no follow-up [C5]. The stronger outcomes were at Beacon, Silverline and Kestrel, where the prospect confirmed a real pain point, the vendor offered a low-commitment, non-demo next step, and the follow-up was tied to a short document or meeting [C2][C3][C4][C6].

claims.text: Beacon Housing Trust (CALL-018, Maya Chen) was the strongest result: Ade Balogun agreed to a meeting in the week of the sixth. OrbitFlow will send technical requirements, Beacon will send its frameworks list, and Ade will bring in Priya Menon. Maya will also check beforehand whether OrbitFlow is on Beacon's procurement frameworks. The meeting was explicitly not a demo.

Silverline Travel (CALL-017, Leo Grant): Martine Duval asked for a short one-page document, not a deck, with Chloe copied. She said that if the page is good Chloe will put a meeting in the diary. Leo had asked for a non-demo 30-minute meeting in the week of the sixth, but no date was confirmed and the meeting is conditional on the page. The follow-up was conditional, and Martine's interest appears moderate.

Kestrel Robotics (CALL-020, Leo Grant): COO Rafael Santos asked for a short, non-deck note on the seven-stage approach and the operations-can-change-it question. He said he would do a 30-minute call if the note is good, and no time was fixed. Leo had proposed a call before mid-October. Rafael declined to restart his Tray.io evaluation.

Quarry Ridge Foods (CALL-016, Maya Chen) produced only a minimal follow-up: Dermot Kelly accepted one email in February 2026 about Power Automate, with no meeting and no further calls this year. He said no new software would be bought this year after an ERP migration, and that Power Automate is already available through the Microsoft deal.

Trafford Dental Group (CALL-019, Alastair McCrae) produced no concrete follow-up. Yvonne Deeks said she would not read any information sent, and concluded OrbitFlow is not a fit. She said her problem is recruitment rather than process, that the price of 1800 pounds a month is far too high, and that the vendor had not asked about her operations and had got facts wrong.

What the successful calls had in common: the prospect confirmed a concrete pain point (Beacon's 26-day void turnaround with no pattern visibility; Silverline's disruption process, 'handled badly'; Kestrel's ERP connector gap and cost of delay). The vendor also asked for a low-commitment next step, explicitly not a demo or pitch, and the vendor conceded weaknesses candidly. For Silverline and Kestrel the follow-up was conditional on a short written piece.

Contrast with the failed calls: at Quarry Ridge the prospect said the pitch 'lands' but they were not looking at anything, which suggests low interest. At Trafford the pitch was generic and missed the prospect's actual problem. At Silverline, the assistant Chloe noted that Martine responds to specifics about the business rather than generic 'workflow automation'.

not_covered: Whether any of the follow-ups (meetings, notes, email) actually happened after the calls.
Cold calls outside CALL-016 to CALL-020.

evidence.context: Martine confirmed that the disruption-event process described by OrbitFlow matches her operation. — Agreement with vendor's description of the problem.

evidence.speaker: Rafael Santos
evidence.quote: Tray don't have a connector and we're looking at building against its API, which our one back-end developer estimates at three weeks.
evidence.context: Prospect's pain point: ERP integration lacks a Tray connector; his one back-end developer estimated three weeks, which he believes will be six. Process changes by operations may wait weeks. — Stated objection/pain relevant to fit; prospect declined to name the ERP.

evidence.speaker: Rafael Santos
evidence.quote: a month is a month of revenue on a two hundred thousand pound order.
evidence.context: Prospect quantified cost of delay: about a month of revenue on a £200k order, with eleven orders in flight. — Business impact relevant to urgency and board case.

evidence.speaker: Maya Chen
evidence.quote: If we get to a demo and it turns out we can't be procured or can't reach your housing system, I've wasted an hour of your life and mine.
evidence.context: Vendor said that a demo would be premature until procurement and system reach were confirmed. — OrbitFlow offer that the first meeting is discovery, not a demo.

evidence.speaker: Maya Chen
evidence.quote: There's a reasonable chance we don't have a native connector for it, and we'd be working through an API or building something.
evidence.context: Vendor flagged that OrbitFlow likely has no native connector for the prospect's housing management system and may need API work at added cost; prospect had assumed as much. — Vendor objection-surfacing; a potential cost and effort barrier.

evidence.speaker: Leo Grant
evidence.quote: If it's a mid-market manufacturing ERP, we probably don't have a native connector
evidence.context: OrbitFlow staff said they probably lack a native connector for the prospect's ERP, so the advantage on that point is none; they claimed only a subtler argument about maintenance and reuse. — Vendor candour; this is a concession, not a claim of superiority.

evidence.speaker: Rafael Santos
evidence.quote: Send me something short — not a deck — on how you'd approach the seven-stage thing, and specifically on the operations-can-change-it question.
evidence.context: The call ended with a concrete follow-up: Leo agreed to send a short written note on the seven-stage approach and the operations-can-change-it question, and Rafael said he would do a thirty-minute call if the note was good; no meeting time was fixed. — Follow-up is conditional on the note being good; Rafael explicitly declined to restart the evaluation. Next step is an email, with a possible 30-minute call before mid-October.

evidence.speaker: Martine Duval
evidence.quote: Send me the page and copy Chloe. If the page is good she'll put it in the diary.
evidence.context: The call ended with a concrete follow-up: Martine asked for a one-page document (not a deck) to be sent and asked Chloe to be copied so it can be put in the diary; Leo requested a 30-minute non-demo meeting in the week of the sixth, and Martine's reply routed that through the page. — Concrete next step agreed, but the meeting itself was conditional on the page being good; no date was confirmed.

claims.text: Contrast with the failed calls: at Quarry Ridge the prospect said the pitch 'lands' but they were not looking at anything, which suggests low interest. At Trafford the pitch was generic and missed the prospect's actual problem. At Silverline, the assistant Chloe noted that Martine responds to specifics about the business rather than generic 'workflow automation'.

evidence.speaker: Dermot Kelly
evidence.quote: It lands. But we're not looking at anything.
evidence.context: Prospect said the pitch resonated but that they are not evaluating anything now; interest level is low for this year. — Mixed signal: tone is polite, but the stated position is no active project.

evidence.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
evidence.quote: you haven't asked me a single question about what we actually do.
evidence.context: Prospect said the group is an 11-practice general dental group and the vendor's facts were wrong (14 practices, referrals direction, no knowledge of NHS e-Referral), and that the vendor did not ask about their operations. — Vendor pitch was generic; prospect corrected factual errors and criticized lack of discovery.

evidence.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
evidence.quote: Recruitment. Dental nurse recruitment. That's my biggest challenge and it has been for two years.
evidence.context: Prospect's biggest challenge is dental nurse recruitment, not a process problem, and the vendor's onboarding automation pitch did not address it. — Prospect rejected the vendor's framing; recruitment is a pay/market issue.

evidence.speaker: Chloe Barnes
evidence.quote: If you say "workflow automation" she'll be polite for a minute and then get off. If you say something about our actual business she'll listen.
evidence.context: Chloe advised that Martine responds to specifics about the business rather than generic workflow automation pitches. — Gatekeeper advice on what engages the decision-maker; the vendor's opener was generic.
